title: Relationships & Social Life
description: Talk about friendships, dating, family dynamics, social events, and interpersonal relationships in Spanish. Learn vocabulary for describing relationships, social interactions, and personal connections.

grammar.title: Conocer vs. Saber — Knowing People vs. Facts
grammar.content:
CONOCER is used for knowing people, places, or being familiar with something:

1. KNOWING PEOPLE:
Conozco a tu hermana. (I know your sister.)
¿Conoces a Maria? (Do you know Maria?)
La conozco desde hace anos. (I've known her for years.)

2. BEING FAMILIAR WITH (places, things):
Conozco Madrid bien. (I know Madrid well.)
Conoces este restaurante? (Do you know this restaurant?)
No conozco esa ciudad. (I don't know that city.)

3. MEETING SOMEONE FOR THE FIRST TIME:
Me llamo Carlos, mucho gusto. Conocerte es un placer. (My name is Carlos, nice to meet you. Meeting you is a pleasure.)

IMPORTANT: When the direct object is a person, use the personal 'a':
Conozco a Pedro. (NOT: Conozco Pedro.)

SABER is used for knowing facts, information, or how to do something:

1. KNOWING FACTS/INFORMATION:
Sabe la respuesta. (He/She knows the answer.)
¿Sabes la hora? (Do you know the time?)
No sé su número de telefono. (I don't know his/her phone number.)

2. KNOWING HOW TO DO SOMETHING (followed by infinitive):
Sé cocinar. (I know how to cook.)
¿Sabes nadar? (Do you know how to swim?)
No sé hablar francés. (I don't know how to speak French.)

3. KNOWING (learned/realized):
Supimos la verdad ayer. (We found out the truth yesterday.)
No sé qué decir. (I don't know what to say.)
examples: Conozco a muchos amigos en esta ciudad. (I know many friends in this city.)
¿Sabes cocinar pasta? (Do you know how to cook pasta?)
Conozco la respuesta, pero no sé explicarla. (I know the answer, but I don't know how to explain it.)
Mi madre conoce a todos los vecinos. (My mother knows all the neighbors.)

grammar.title: Quedar — Making Plans and Arranging Meetings
grammar.content:
Quedar is one of the most common verbs used for making plans in Spanish:

1. MEETING UP (reflexive: quedar):
Quedamos a las ocho. (We meet at eight.)
¿Quedamos mañana? (Shall we meet tomorrow?)
Nos quedamos en el centro. (We'll meet in the center.)

2. ARRANGING TO MEET (con + lugar/persona):
Quedo con mis amigos el sábado. (I'm meeting my friends on Saturday.)
Quedamos en el café de la plaza. (We'll meet at the café in the square.)

3. COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
Quedar bien/mal (to look good/bad on someone)
Quedar embarazada (to get pregnant)
Quedar en algo (to agree on something)

4. CONJUGATION (present indicative):
Quedar: yo quedo, tú quedas, él/ella queda, nosotros quedamos, vosotros quedáis, ellos quedan
Quedo, quedas, queda, quedamos, quedáis, quedan

5. USING QUEDAR FOR DATE PLANS:
¿Quedamos esta noche? (Shall we meet tonight?)
Quedamos a las nueve en el cine. (We'll meet at nine at the cinema.)
Quedamos para cenar. (We'll meet for dinner.)
examples: ¿Quedamos el viernes por la tarde? (Shall we meet Friday afternoon?)
Quedamos en la plaza mayor. (We'll meet in the main square.)
Nos quedamos con Marta después del trabajo. (We're meeting Marta after work.)
Quedamos en ir al restaurante nuevo. (We agreed to go to the new restaurant.)

grammar.title: Reflexive Verbs for Relationships — Sentirse, Preocuparse, Enamorarse
grammar.content:
REFLEXIVE VERBS show actions that the subject does to themself. They are very common in relationship contexts:

1. SENTIRSE (to feel — emotions):
Me siento feliz. (I feel happy.)
Te sientes triste. (You feel sad.)
Se siente cansado. (He feels tired.)

2. PREOCUPARSE DE (to worry about):
Me preocupo por mis hijos. (I worry about my children.)
Te preocupas demasiado. (You worry too much.)
Nos preocupa el futuro. (We worry about the future.)

3. ENAMORARSE DE (to fall in love with):
Me enamoré de ti. (I fell in love with you.)
Se enamoraron en la universidad. (They fell in love at university.)
Nos enamoramos el primer dia. (We fell in love on the first day.)

4. PELEARSE CON (to argue/fight with):
Me peleo con mi hermano a veces. (I fight with my brother sometimes.)
Se pelearon por una tonteria. (They fought over something silly.)

5. PERDONARSE / PEDIR PERDÓN:
Te perdono. (I forgive you.)
Pido perdón. (I apologize.)
Se perdonaron después de la discusión. (They forgave each other after the argument.)

Common reflexive relationship verbs:
- sentirse = to feel
- preocuparse = to worry
- enamorarse = to fall in love
- pelearse = to fight
- disculparse = to apologize
- encontrar(se) = to meet
- llamar(se) = to call oneself
examples: Me siento bien con ella. (I feel good with her.)
Se preocupan mucho por los niños. (They worry a lot about the kids.)
Nos enamoramos el verano pasado. (We fell in love last summer.)
Me peleo con mi novia, pero luego nos perdonamos. (I fight with my girlfriend, but then we forgive each other.)

grammar.title: Describing People and Relationships — Adjectives and Expressions
grammar.content:
Spanish has many adjectives for describing personality traits and relationship qualities. These often need to agree in gender and number:

1. POSITIVE TRAITS:
Sincero/a — sincere
Generoso/a — generous
Simpatico/a — nice/pleasant
Amistoso/a — friendly
Sociable — sociable
Leal — loyal
Responsable — responsible
Trabajador/a — hardworking
Diverso/a — fun/entertaining
Comprensivo/a — understanding

2. NEGATIVE TRAITS:
Celoso/a — jealous
Perezoso/a — lazy
Egoista — selfish
Tacaño/a — stingy
Mentiroso/a — liar
Arrogante — arrogant

3. RELATIONSHIP STATUS:
Soltero/a — single
Comprometido/a — engaged
Casado/a — married
Divorciado/a — divorced
Separado/a — separated
Viudo/a — widowed

4. AGREEMENT RULES:
Adjectives must match the gender and number of the noun they describe:
Mi amigo es simpatico. (My friend is nice — masculine)
Mi amiga es simpatica. (My friend is nice — feminine)
Mis amigos son simpaticos. (My friends are nice — masculine plural)
Mis amigas son simpaticas. (My friends are nice — feminine plural)

5. USING MUCHO/POCO:
Es muy simpatico. (He is very nice.)
Es bastante generoso. (He is quite generous.)
Es poco sociable. (He is not very sociable.)
Es demasiado celoso. (He is too jealous.)
examples: Mi mejor amigo es muy sincero y generoso. (My best friend is very sincere and generous.)
Ella es una persona muy sociable y divertida. (She is a very sociable and fun person.)
Son solteros y disfrutan de su libertad. (They are single and enjoy their freedom.)
Mi hermano es un poco celoso, pero es muy leal. (My brother is a bit jealous, but he is very loyal.)

pronunciation.title: Relationship Vocabulary — Key Sounds and Stress
pronunciation.content:
Spanish pronunciation in relationship contexts:

1. THE LETTER 'Ñ' (eñe) — unique Spanish sound:
- amigo NO es 'amigno' — it's a-mi-go (with soft g like 'h')
- amigo NO tiene 'ñ' — the 'ñ' sound is like 'ny' in 'onion'
- words with ñ: amigo (no ñ), hermano (has ñ) -> her-MAH-no

2. STRESS IN RELATIONSHIP WORDS:
- rela-cion (stress on last syllable: re-la-CEON)
- amigo (stress on last syllable: a-MI-go)
- novio (stress on last syllable: NO-vyo)
- novia (stress on first syllable: NO-vya)
- pareja (stress on second syllable: pa-RE-ha)

3. THE 'G' SOUND (hard vs soft):
Hard G (like English 'g'): gusto, gente, regalo
Soft G (like English 'h'): amigo, amigo, ligero, enemigo

4. THE 'LL' AND 'Y' SOUND (yeísmo):
In most Spanish dialects, ll and y sound the same:
- llama -> YAH-ma
- yo -> yoh
- llamar -> yah-MAHR
- llamar -> to call

5. COMMON PHRASES — FULL SENTENCES:
- Me llamo Carlos y soy de Mexico. -> meh YAH-moh KAH-lohs y soys deh meh-KSEE-koh
- Quiero mucho a mi familia. -> KYEH-ro MOO-choh ah mee fah-MEE-lyah
- Nos vemos mañana. -> nohs BEH-moh mah-nyAH-nah

examples.source: reh-lah-see-OWN — stress on last syllable, accent on ó
keh-REHR — q always followed by u

pronunciation.title: Intonation in Questions About Relationships
pronunciation.content:
Spanish questions about relationships follow specific intonation patterns:

1. YES/NO QUESTIONS (rising intonation):
¿Conoces a Maria? (Do you know Maria?) — voice goes up at the end
¿Salen juntos? (Do they go out together?) — voice goes up at the end
¿Están comprometidos? (Are they engaged?) — voice goes up at the end

2. QUESTIONS WITH QUESTION WORDS (falling intonation):
¿Quién es tu mejor amigo? (Who is your best friend?) — voice falls at the end
¿Dónde quedan? (Where do they meet?) — voice falls at the end
¿Cuándo se conocieron? (When did they meet?) — voice falls at the end
¿Por qué se pelearon? (Why did they fight?) — voice falls at the end

3. EXPRESSING EMOTION IN SPEECH:
- When expressing love: softer tone, slower pace
- When talking about a fight: sharper, faster pace
- When asking about someone: curious, rising intonation

4. COMMON QUESTION PATTERNS:
¿Cómo se llaman? (What are their names?)
¿De dónde son? (Where are they from?)
¿Desde cuándo se conocen? (How long have they known each other?)

examples.source: Do you know your partner? (rising intonation)
Who is your favorite friend? (falling intonation)
How long have they been together? (falling intonation)

exercises.question: Which verb should you use for 'I know Maria' (I am familiar with Maria as a person)?
exercises.explanation: Conocer is used for knowing people. Always use the personal 'a' before a specific person: 'Conozco a Maria.'

exercises.question: Complete: '___ sé cómo cocinar, pero sé la receta. (I don't know how to cook, but I know the recipe.)'
exercises.explanation: No sé cómo cocinar = I don't know how to cook (saber + infinitive for ability). 'Pero sé la receta' = but I know the recipe (saber a fact).

exercises.question: How do you say 'We meet at eight' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Quedamos = we meet up (from quedar). 'Quedamos a las ocho' = We meet at eight o'clock.

exercises.question: Which adjective means 'friendly' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Amistoso/a = friendly. Celoso = jealous, simpático = nice/pleasant, responsable = responsible.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Me ___ de ti. (I fell in love with you.)'
exercises.explanation: Enamorarse de = to fall in love with. 'Me enamoré de ti' = I fell in love with you (past tense, reflexive).

exercises.question: What does 'soltero/a' mean?
exercises.explanation: Soltero/a = single. Married = casado/a, engaged = comprometido/a, divorced = divorciado/a.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Quedamos ___ el café del centro. (We'll meet at the café in the center.)'
exercises.explanation: Quedar en + place = to meet at a place. 'Quedamos en el café' = We'll meet at the café.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct for 'I worry about my children'?
exercises.explanation: Preocuparse de/con + por = to worry about. 'Me preocupo por mis hijos' = I worry about my children.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Mi hermano es muy ___ pero también es leal. (My brother is very jealous but he is also loyal.)'
exercises.explanation: Celoso/a = jealous. 'Mi hermano es muy celoso' = My brother is very jealous.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'Do you know how to swim?'
exercises.explanation: Saber + infinitive = to know how to do something. '¿Sabes nadar?' = Do you know how to swim?

exercises.question: Complete: '___ siento muy bien con mi mejor amiga. (I feel very good with my best friend.)'
exercises.explanation: Sentirse = to feel (oneself). 'Me siento' = I feel (reflexive pronoun me + conjugated sentir).

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'They are engaged'?
exercises.explanation: Comprometido/a = engaged. 'Están comprometidos' = They are engaged (masculine or mixed group).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Se ___ después de la discusión. (They forgave each other after the argument.)'
exercises.explanation: Perdonarse = to forgive each other. 'Se perdonaron' = They forgave each other (past tense, reflexive).

exercises.question: How do you say 'My best friend is very sincere' in Spanish?
options: Mi mejor amigo es muy sincero
Mi mejor amigo es muy sincera
Mi mejor amiga es muy sincero
exercises.explanation: The adjective must match the noun. 'Amigo' is masculine, so 'sincero' (not 'sincera'). 'Mi mejor amigo es muy sincero.'

exercises.question: Complete: '¿Quedamos esta noche para ___? (Shall we meet tonight for dinner?)'
exercises.explanation: Cenar = to have dinner. 'Quedamos para cenar' = Shall we meet for dinner?
